title: Nilpotent derived reduction detects upper bounds for ordinary modules in arbitrary carrier universes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring in $\mathrm{Type}\,u$, let $I$ be an ideal, and let $N\geq1$ satisfy $I^N=0$. Use $A$-modules with carriers in $\mathrm{Type}(\max(u,v))$ and derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with independently specified hom universes. Let $L:D(A)\to D(A/I)$ be any total left derived functor of extension of scalars, specified by its universal counit [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For $C\in D(A)$ and $b\in\mathbf Z$, if $H^i(L(C))=0$ for every $i>b$, then $H^i(C)=0$ for every $i>b$.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, upper-bound-only filtration argument used in Tag 09AR, lemma-lift-complex-projectives

proof.text: Let A' = ULift A in the carrier universe and let a : A ≃+* A' be the lift ring isomorphism. Put J = a(I); the identity map(I^N) = map(I)^N gives J^N = 0. The quotient ring isomorphism q : A/I ≃+* A'/J is given by q(mk(x)) = mk(a(x)).

Evaluation at the unique object gives an additive exact equivalence from RingSiteModules A' [def-pc-ring-hom-extension-shared-definitions] to A'-modules. It is full by extending a module map to each object, faithful because all objects are the unique object, and essentially surjective via constant module presheaves. Every presheaf is a sheaf for the bottom topology. The sheafification adjunction unit is invertible here, so it gives a natural isomorphism identifying evaluated site scalar extension with ordinary scalar extension. Compose evaluation with restriction of scalars along a and q. The scalar-extension square is the adjunction mate of the equality of the restriction-of-scalars composites induced by q(mk(x)) = mk(a(x)).

Choose standard derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] on the two sites, with a common hom universe, and obtain the site derived pair from [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Precomposition by the induced homotopy equivalence preserves its right Kan universal property. The exact-functor factorization Qh composed with D(eA) identifies the two localization functors. Postcomposition by the derived equivalence D(eB) preserves the right Kan universal property, since it induces an equivalence of the categories of right extensions. The scalar-extension natural isomorphism identifies the functors being derived. Uniqueness yields D(eA) composed with L isomorphic to LF composed with D(eB), allowing the supplied ordinary derived categories to have independent hom universes.

Let C' be the inverse image of C under D(eA). The comparison just constructed and the counit isomorphism D(eA)(C') ≅ C identify D(eB)(LF(C')) with L(C). Exact functors commute with cohomology. Apply the inverse equivalence eB to transport hred to vanishing for LF(C'). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-derived-upper-bound] to J, N and C'. Apply eA and its cohomology comparison to transport the resulting vanishing back to C. The construction uses no finiteness or bounded-below assumptions and applies also to I = 0 and the zero ring.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0H75 upper-bound adaptation used by Tag 09AR; explicit equivalence and universe transport of lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-derived-upper-bound

theorem isZero_homology_of_nilpotent_module_reduction
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (N : ℕ)
    (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hI : I ^ N = ⊥)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A ⧸ I))]
    (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A ⧸ I)))
    (ε : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L ⟶
      @Functor.mapHomotopyCategory _ _ _ _ _ _ _
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))
        (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).left_adjoint_additive
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)
    [L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (b : ℤ)
    (hred : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A ⧸ I)) i).obj (L.obj C))) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj C)
